title: Choose the visual world for Brett Sabol Plumbing
question: Bolder hand, as asked. This is the fourth hand. If none fits, please type in the steer box what is missing (more photos, more like the trucks, darker, cleaner, more premium) before re-rolling, so the next hand aims at it.

options.label: Arcade Cabinet
options.lineage: Pixel-art arcade cabinets, scanlines and phosphor glow
options.thesis: The plumber everyone grew up with wore red and blue. So does Brett, and his site plays like the cabinet.
options.viewport: A cabinet screen: pixel-cap HUD with the license and 24 hour line, a pixel sprite of the real box truck crossing the tiles, SELECT SERVICE as a stage menu, and PRESS CALL 215.666.3086 as the giant pixel button.
options.risk: It can read as a joke on a family business, and the famous red and blue plumber is someone else's trademark, so no warp pipes, mushrooms or coins.

raised.raise: Depth only by overlapping flat color layers, never by shading or glow gradients behind text.
One long column in Brett's own order: the owner's story runs top to bottom, no grid of equal boxes.
One line rules the layout: a single run of pipe sprite carries the eye from the hero down every page.

options.label: Service Timetable
options.lineage: The pocket transit timetable, here the SEPTA schedule every Trevose commuter carries
options.thesis: Brett's hours, areas and services set like the timetable for the line that stops a mile from his shop.
materials: one type size, weight and case for rank
options.viewport: Goldenrod ground, a huge condensed headline, a slate SERVICE BOARD listing office hours, weekend appointments and the 24 hour line as timetable rows, and a working request form beside it with service, town and phone.
options.case: Beats the arcade on both axes: locals know this timetable from their own commute, and hours, areas and emergency availability are literally schedule information.
options.risk: Yellow ground and one type size are loud, and the transit idea turns into a costume the moment a row stops carrying real information.

options.label: Nixie Line
options.thesis: The phone number glows in tubes like a lab instrument: the one number that matters, lit.
options.viewport: A steel panel where 215 666 3086 glows in nixie tubes as the call button, with the license number and 24 hour line in smaller banks and engraved labels below.
options.case: Holds product clarity, the phone number could not be clearer, but nobody in Bucks County identifies with a lab counter.
options.risk: Tube banks invite counters, which the brand rules forbid, so only real numbers may ever glow. Dark retro-lab mood.

options.label: Fan Shrine
options.lineage: Single-subject fan pages of the early web
options.thesis: One devoted column with tiled background.
options.viewport: Centered table over a star tile with a hit counter.
options.case: Its signature is a hit counter, and fake counters are banned. Loses both axes.
options.kept: One long column in the owner's own order.

options.label: Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Depth from pasted layers of flat color.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel built from layers.
options.case: Folk craft says gift shop, not Master Plumber. Loses both axes.
options.kept: Depth only by overlap, never by shading.

options.label: Curved Crease
options.thesis: One sweeping fold lifts a flat sheet into a shell.
options.viewport: A cream disc lifting along one charcoal arc.
options.case: Cream paper and italic serif is the exact look you rejected before. Loses both axes.
options.kept: One line rules the whole layout.
options.risk: The AI-default cream and serif rut.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The premium plumber site played straight, at the craft level of Roto-Rooter, Benjamin Franklin Plumbing and Mr. Rooter.
canonCard.viewport: The van photo with headline and two buttons at left, a trust row of verified credentials, and service cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
